improvement_directive: Supply the missing positive-band converse at the n^{-t} scale on R_pair by redoing the KBRW-style two-point/Assouad construction with the design density held uniform (hence trivially inside [f_-,f_+]) and the separation carried entirely by unequal-resolution, mean-zero perturbations of pi_P and mu_{a,P} at resolutions ell ~ n^{-t/(2s)} and h ~ n^{-t/gamma}, verifying Holder membership, the n^{-t} target separation at x_0, and a bounded n-sample Hellinger/chi-square mixture distance; failing that, extend the close-pair upper bound off the alpha<=1, beta<alpha subregion (higher-order pair differences for alpha>1) so the achievability covers the full low-smoothness region.
critique: What is actually proved is a one-sided achievability result: a pair-difference U-statistic local R-estimator attains the ALREADY-PUBLISHED KBRW exponent t = (1 + d/(2gamma) + d/(4s))^{-1}, so the rate itself is not new; the only new content is that the estimator needs no density estimator and no density smoothness, and only on the proper subregion R_pair = R_low ∩ {0<beta<alpha<=1}. The advertised 'positive-band minimax bracket' c n^{-q} <= R_n <= C n^{-t} is not a frontier: its lower endpoint is the textbook two-point pointwise-regression bound n^{-gamma/(2gamma+d)}, proved with a fixed uniform density and constant propensity 1/2, which says nothing whatsoever about the density band or the nuisance-smoothness bottleneck the note is named for, and the two endpoints have strictly different exponents (t<q), so nothing about the band-only exponent is determined. thm:density-coupled-lower-bound is a verbatim restatement of lem:oracle-regression-lower-bound, and def:density-coupled-handle / def:asymmetric-frontier-handle are labels for unexecuted programs that prove nothing, so the note is smaller than its section count suggests. The entire novelty claim rests on the unverified Related-Work assertion that the KBRW lower construction 'has support holes and therefore is not a converse for the present fixed-positive-band class' — this is stated with no theorem, lemma, or page citation, yet if false the frontier is already closed and the note reduces to a re-derivation. Minor but real: lem:matrix-bernstein is stated as a bare uncited leaf (Tropp 2012 appears only in the bibliography), the estimator is non-adaptive in (alpha,beta,gamma), and the definition of D_{ij} in def:close-pair-r-estimator contains a broken macro (',qquad') that would fail to compile.
